threats.name: Use After Free
threats.rationale: Use after free needs manual deallocation. Java objects are reclaimed by the garbage collector only when unreachable, so a live reference never dangles. The residual route is native memory (JNI, Unsafe, foreign-memory API), which the library does not use.

closed_by.detail: No `native` method, no System.load/loadLibrary, no sun.misc.Unsafe, jdk.internal.misc, java.lang.foreign or JNI/JNA use in the library sources, so the memory-safety guarantee of the JVM is not bypassed.

The JVM verifies bytecode, checks every array index and null dereference, and has no pointer arithmetic; a memory error in pure Java surfaces as an exception, not corruption. A statement about the runtime, not a check on the package, and it holds only if no JNI, Unsafe or foreign-memory use exists (the analyzer rule).
